PyTorch `MultiheadAttention` accepts floating `attn_mask` tensors shaped `(L,L)` or `(B*num_heads,L,L)` for self-attention; values add to attention logits before softmax. This supports learned additive biases mathematically, provided their construction preserves autograd. Use `need_weights=False` to enable the optimized SDPA path; it does not disable gradients. When supplying both attention and padding masks, match their types; float padding masks can use zero for valid keys and negative infinity for padding. Boolean `True` means blocked in MHA, whereas direct SDPA uses `True` for allowed positions. [MHA documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.activation.MultiheadAttention.html), [SDPA documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention)

SDPA selects implementations according to inputs and backend availability; `need_weights=False` does not guarantee FlashAttention or support for bias gradients in every fused backend. Use `torch.nn.attention.sdpa_kernel` to investigate eligibility, and verify finite, nonzero bias gradients on the host’s installed version. A materialized dense bias alone requires `B*num_heads*L²*element_size` bytes; inference from tensor dimensions, excluding gradient storage, mask merging and attention intermediates. Broadcasting may reduce initial storage, but subsequent operations can materialize tensors. Measure representative forward/backward latency and peak allocated GPU memory before committing training budget. Documentation establishes API behavior, not actual overhead for this workload. [SDPA backend guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention)
